title: Authenticated Web and API Security with OWASP ZAP
tagline: A sign-in page is not the application. Test the authorized and denied paths behind it.
problem: A workforce platform used Microsoft sign-in and role-protected APIs. An anonymous web scan could inspect the public shell yet never reach the routes where staff permissions mattered. Test tokens and response bodies also needed protection from reports.
solution: Use a pinned ZAP image and a fixed passive ten-GET matrix for anonymous, Admin and Caregiver-only identities. Verify exact identity/role before protected probes, refuse redirects/arbitrary routes and summarize only fixed alert metadata.
outcome: Recorded nonproduction acceptance exercised ten GETs across four handlers, with two informational cache observations and no Low/Medium/High alerts in that bounded sample. It was not whole-application clearance.
strengths: Inspect real requests/responses, including headers and behavior that package/IaC scanners cannot observe.
Reach explicitly selected paths after sign-in, then compare authorized and lower-privilege behavior.
Observe selected traffic without injecting active attack payloads; combine exact role assertions with safe alert summaries.
tests: Nine original Python contract tests passed. The fictional probe exercises the actual ten-request evaluator.
limit: No new hosted scan, token collection or Microsoft sign-in was performed. The public target is deliberately api.workforce.invalid.
diagram:
Browser[Fresh authorized sign-in] --> Token[Private short-lived tokens]
  Token --> Matrix[Fixed ten-GET matrix]
  Matrix --> ZAP[Pinned passive ZAP proxy]
  ZAP --> API[Reviewed API handlers]
  API --> Claims[Identity / role / expected status]
  ZAP --> Summary[Alert IDs / risk / counts only]
